description_good: README.md describes what the software does (end-to-end encrypted, offline-first personal and family finance tracker with multi-device sync), with an English summary: https://github.com/tsudev-org/qulythuchi/blob/main/README.md
interact: README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md and the issue forms explain how to obtain the source, build and test it, report bugs, request features and contribute: https://github.com/tsudev-org/qulythuchi/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution: CONTRIBUTING.md explains the pull request process (squash-merged pull requests into main): https://github.com/tsudev-org/qulythuchi/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution_requirements: CONTRIBUTING.md lists the requirements: Conventional Commits, tests with every behaviour change, integer money, libsodium-only cryptography with versioned envelopes, security review for crypto/sync/sign-in changes, and every CI check green: https://github.com/tsudev-org/qulythuchi/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
floss_license_osi: AGPL-3.0 is OSI approved; GitHub detects the license as AGPL-3.0.
license_location: The license is in the standard location LICENSE at the repository root: https://github.com/tsudev-org/qulythuchi/blob/main/LICENSE
documentation_basics: README.md (overview, status), CONTRIBUTING.md (how to build and run the tests), docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (components and data flow), docs/FEATURES.md and the architecture decision records in docs/adr/: https://github.com/tsudev-org/qulythuchi/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md
documentation_interface: The external interfaces are documented: the sync server HTTP API (/api/v1/...) and its error codes in docs/adr/0010-may-chu-dong-bo-p5.md and later ADRs (0015 shared wallets, 0016/0018/0019 TsuDEV Pro, 0017 attachments), and the encrypted envelope format with machine-checkable vectors in conformance/envelope-v1.json: https://github.com/tsudev-org/qulythuchi/blob/main/docs/adr/0010-may-chu-dong-bo-p5.md
sites_https: The project website https://qulythuchi.tsudev.com (including the web app and the sync API) and the repository are HTTPS only, with HSTS max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains; preload.
discussion: GitHub Issues and pull requests are public, searchable, URL-addressable and open to anyone with a GitHub account: https://github.com/tsudev-org/qulythuchi/issues
english: README.md and SECURITY.md have English summaries, CONTRIBUTING.md is in English, and the issue forms accept reports in English or Vietnamese: https://github.com/tsudev-org/qulythuchi/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
maintained: Actively maintained: dozens of pull requests merged in the last month: https://github.com/tsudev-org/qulythuchi/pulls?q=is%3Apr+is%3Amerged
repo_public: Public git repository on GitHub: https://github.com/tsudev-org/qulythuchi
repo_track: git records who changed what and when; every change is a reviewed pull request with a description: https://github.com/tsudev-org/qulythuchi/commits/main
repo_interim: Every change, including work in progress, is pushed to branches and merged into main through pull requests in the public repository: https://github.com/tsudev-org/qulythuchi/pulls?q=is%3Apr
repo_distributed: git (a distributed version control system) on GitHub.
version_unique: The web app and sync server are deployed continuously; every production deployment of main gets a unique tag deploy-YYYY.MM.DD.N, created automatically after the deploy by scripts/release-tag.mjs: https://github.com/tsudev-org/qulythuchi/tags . Installable app releases (not published yet) will use the ecosystem version YY.M.DDNN (e.g. 26.11.1701, shown in Settings > About).
version_semver: Deployments use Calendar Versioning YYYY.MM.DD with a counter .N for several deployments on the same day (e.g. deploy-2026.11.20.1); app versions use the ecosystem CalVer YY.M.DDNN. The deploy- prefix keeps web deployments apart from app release tags (vYY.M.DDNN).
version_tags: Each production deployment is an annotated git tag on the deployed main commit: https://github.com/tsudev-org/qulythuchi/tags (script: https://github.com/tsudev-org/qulythuchi/blob/main/scripts/release-tag.mjs, run by the postdeploy step of services/sync-api)
release_notes: Each version has human-readable release notes: the annotated tag message lists every change merged since the previous deployment (shown at https://github.com/tsudev-org/qulythuchi/tags), and CHANGELOG.md summarises the changes in plain language: https://github.com/tsudev-org/qulythuchi/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md
release_notes_vulns: No vulnerability with a CVE or similar public identifier has been fixed in this project. Such fixes would be named in the release notes and CHANGELOG.md and published as a GitHub Security Advisory (SECURITY.md).
report_process: Bug reports go to GitHub Issues using the bug report form: https://github.com/tsudev-org/qulythuchi/issues/new/choose
report_tracker: GitHub Issues with bug report and feature request forms: https://github.com/tsudev-org/qulythuchi/issues
report_responses: No external bug report has been filed so far (young project); the maintainer reads every issue and acknowledges reports within days.
enhancement_responses: No external enhancement request has been filed so far; the feature request form routes them to the maintainer, who answers each one.
report_archive: GitHub Issues are public and searchable: https://github.com/tsudev-org/qulythuchi/issues?q=is%3Aissue
vulnerability_report_process: SECURITY.md describes how to report vulnerabilities (English section included): https://github.com/tsudev-org/qulythuchi/blob/main/SECURITY.md
vulnerability_report_private: GitHub private vulnerability reporting is enabled: https://github.com/tsudev-org/qulythuchi/security/advisories/new
vulnerability_report_response: No vulnerability report was received in the last 6 months. SECURITY.md commits to a reply within 7 days and a fix for serious issues within 30 days.
build: Standard builds: flutter build (Android, iOS, macOS, Windows, Linux, web), dart pub for the core package, npm ci + wrangler for the sync server, Astro for the website; scripts/build-web.sh builds the full site. CI builds Linux, web, iOS and macOS on every pull request: https://github.com/tsudev-org/qulythuchi/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
build_common_tools: Standard tools: Flutter/Dart, npm, the TypeScript compiler, wrangler (Cloudflare Workers), Astro, Xcode for Apple targets.
build_floss_tools: Flutter, Dart, Node.js, npm, TypeScript, wrangler/workerd and Astro are FLOSS. (Building for iOS/macOS additionally needs Xcode, which is only required for those targets.)
test: Automated test suites: packages/core (dart test: money, crypto envelopes, recovery phrase, sharing, sync records), apps/app (flutter test: about 130 unit and widget tests, two screen sizes), services/sync-api (vitest running the Worker in workerd with D1/R2: 81 tests), plus cross-implementation crypto vectors checked against an independent libsodium: https://github.com/tsudev-org/qulythuchi/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
test_invocation: Standard invocations: dart test, flutter test, npm test (documented in CONTRIBUTING.md): https://github.com/tsudev-org/qulythuchi/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
test_most: Tests cover the encryption envelopes and key hierarchy (tamper, wrong key/context, nonce uniqueness, BIP39 vectors), money arithmetic, sync conflicts and rollback/identity-change detection, shared wallet key sharing, the server authorization and Pro gate, the attachment pipeline and the main user flows.
test_continuous_integration: GitHub Actions runs every test suite, format/lint/analyze, the conformance check, Linux and web builds on every pull request and push to main, and iOS/macOS builds with simulator runs: https://github.com/tsudev-org/qulythuchi/blob/main/.github/workflows/ci.yml
test_policy: CONTRIBUTING.md: every change in behaviour comes with tests in the same pull request; a bug fix comes with a regression test that fails without the fix: https://github.com/tsudev-org/qulythuchi/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
tests_are_added: Recent changes add tests with the code, e.g. #36 (TsuDEV Pro in the app: 25 tests + server tests), #32 (encrypted receipt attachments), #34 (verified purge): https://github.com/tsudev-org/qulythuchi/pull/36
tests_documented_added: The test requirement is written in CONTRIBUTING.md (Pull request requirements, point 2): https://github.com/tsudev-org/qulythuchi/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
warnings: Dart/Flutter analyzer with flutter_lints and strict-casts/strict-inference/strict-raw-types (apps/app/analysis_options.yaml); TypeScript strict mode and typescript-eslint strictTypeChecked for the server: https://github.com/tsudev-org/qulythuchi/blob/main/apps/app/analysis_options.yaml
warnings_fixed: CI runs dart analyze / flutter analyze with --fatal-infos and ESLint + tsc for the server, so every warning (even info level) fails the build and is fixed before merge.
warnings_strict: Analyzer strict modes are enabled and --fatal-infos treats even informational lints as errors; TypeScript strict + strictTypeChecked ESLint rules.
know_secure_design: The maintainer documented the design and threat model: assets, trust boundaries and threats T1-T31 with mitigations (end-to-end encryption, server never trusted with plaintext, fail-closed authorization, least privilege): https://github.com/tsudev-org/qulythuchi/blob/main/docs/THREAT_MODEL.md
know_common_errors: docs/THREAT_MODEL.md and the per-change security reviews in docs/security-reviews/ (OWASP Top 10 checklist) cover common errors and their mitigations: injection (parameterised SQL), XSS (strict CSP, no HTML rendering of user data), CSRF (SameSite cookies + header check), SSRF, broken access control, insecure randomness and secrets in logs: https://github.com/tsudev-org/qulythuchi/blob/main/docs/security-reviews/20261120-t7-app-pro.md
crypto_published: Only published algorithms: Argon2id, XChaCha20-Poly1305, X25519, X-Wing (ML-KEM-768 + X25519), BLAKE2b, SHA-256, ECDSA P-256 (ES256) for tokens, and TLS.
crypto_call: No primitives are implemented in the project: the app calls libsodium (sodium package), the server uses WebCrypto and jose. ADR-0002 forbids custom cryptography: https://github.com/tsudev-org/qulythuchi/blob/main/docs/adr/0002-ma-hoa-dau-cuoi-phan-cap-khoa.md
crypto_floss: All cryptographic libraries (libsodium via the sodium Dart package and libsodium.js on the web, SQLite3MultipleCiphers for the encrypted local database, jose, workerd WebCrypto/BoringSSL) are FLOSS.
crypto_keylength: 256-bit symmetric keys (XChaCha20-Poly1305), X25519 and ML-KEM-768 (hybrid X-Wing), ECDSA P-256, Argon2id with 64 MiB / 3 passes by default (unlock refuses parameters below the OWASP floor of 19 MiB / 2 passes); TLS is terminated by Cloudflare with modern key lengths.
crypto_working: No broken or weak algorithms (MD5, SHA-1, DES, RC4, ECB) are used anywhere for security.
crypto_weaknesses: No default security mechanism depends on an algorithm with known serious weaknesses.
crypto_pfs: HTTPS is terminated by Cloudflare with TLS 1.3/1.2 ECDHE key exchange only, which provides perfect forward secrecy; the apps pin the TLS roots.
crypto_password_storage: The project does not store passwords for authenticating users: sign-in is delegated to tsudev.com via OIDC. The local encryption password is never stored; it only derives keys with Argon2id and a per-account random salt.
crypto_random: Keys, nonces, salts, tokens and installation ids use a CSPRNG: libsodium randombytes in the app, crypto.getRandomValues in the server (https://github.com/tsudev-org/qulythuchi/blob/main/services/sync-api/src/lib/crypto.ts). Math.random is only used to sample when to run housekeeping, never for security.
delivery_mitm: The website, web app and API are served over HTTPS only with HSTS preload, a strict CSP and Subresource-free self-hosted assets; the apps pin TLS roots. Source is delivered by GitHub over HTTPS/SSH.
delivery_unsigned: Hashes are never retrieved over plain HTTP. Web assets fetched at build time (sodium.js, sqlite3.wasm) are verified against SHA-256 checksums pinned in the repository (apps/app/tool/fetch_web_assets.sh).
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days: No unpatched vulnerability of medium or higher severity: 0 open Dependabot alerts and 0 open CodeQL alerts; npm audit runs in CI. (Open code-scanning entries are only OpenSSF Scorecard posture findings, not vulnerabilities.)
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed: No critical vulnerability has been reported or is open.
no_leaked_credentials: No valid credentials in the repository: gitleaks scans every push and pull request, GitHub secret scanning with push protection is enabled, and secrets live only in Cloudflare secrets / local files outside git.
static_analysis: CodeQL (GitHub default setup) on every push and pull request, OpenSSF Scorecard, the Dart analyzer with strict modes and ESLint strictTypeChecked: https://github.com/tsudev-org/qulythuchi/security/code-scanning
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities: CodeQL security queries for JavaScript/TypeScript look for injection, XSS, SSRF, insecure randomness, regex DoS and similar vulnerabilities (e.g. a CodeQL finding about double-decoding HTML entities in the email importer was fixed, CHANGELOG.md).
static_analysis_fixed: 0 open CodeQL alerts; findings are fixed before release (e.g. HTML entities in forwarded email are now decoded in a single pass).
static_analysis_often: CodeQL runs on every push and pull request; the analyzers run in CI on every pull request.
dynamic_analysis: No dedicated dynamic analysis tool (fuzzer or web scanner) is used yet. The test suites do exercise the running server in workerd and tampered/random inputs for the crypto envelopes, but we do not claim that as dynamic analysis.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe: No memory-unsafe language is part of the project code: Dart and TypeScript only (libsodium and SQLCipher are upstream libraries).
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions: Tests run with assertions enabled (dart test and flutter test enable assert by default; vitest expectations), and runtime checks such as the money overflow guard stay on in production.
dynamic_analysis_fixed: No dynamic analysis tool is used yet (see dynamic_analysis), so no vulnerability has been found by one.
